title: Dimension of a finite type domain over a field equals the transcendence degree of its fraction field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be its fraction field. Then the Krull dimension of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and the transcendence degree of $K$ over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] are finite and equal: $$\dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K.$$ Moreover, for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$, the local ring $A_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has this same dimension.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P0 (label lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, lines 28171-28191); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00P0,algebra-lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring)

proof.text: Apply the finite-type domain local-dimension theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring]. It supplies a natural number d with ringKrullDim S = d and identifies the dimension of every maximal localization with d.
The Mathlib theorem Algebra.trdeg_eq_of_ringKrullDim_eq applies to the finite-type domain S and the equality ringKrullDim S = d, yielding Algebra.trdeg k S = d.

Equip FractionRing S with its induced k-algebra structure and the scalar tower k → S → FractionRing S. Localization makes FractionRing S algebraic over S, so trdeg S (FractionRing S) = 0. The Mathlib identity trdeg_add_eq then gives trdeg k (FractionRing S) = trdeg k S + 0 = trdeg k S.
Combining the preceding equalities gives Algebra.trdeg k (FractionRing S) = d, while the localization equality from the first step gives the final assertion for every maximal ideal.
